cues.speaker: ER
cues.text: Hello William.

cues.speaker: ER
cues.text: This is Amber – you said to phone if I wanted to get more information about the job

cues.speaker: ER
cues.text: agency you mentioned. Is now a good time?

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: Oh, hi Amber. Yes. Fine.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: So the agency I was talking about is called Bankside – they're based in Docklands – I can

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: tell you the address now – 497 Eastside.

cues.speaker: ER
cues.text: OK, thanks. So is there anyone in particular I should speak to there?

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: The agent I always deal with is called Becky Jamieson.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: Yes, it's in my contacts somewhere – right, here we are: 078 double 6, 510 triple 3.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: I wouldn't call her until the afternoon if I were you – she's always really busy in the

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: morning trying to fill last-minute vacancies.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: She's really helpful and friendly so I'm sure it would be worth getting in touch with her

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: for an informal chat.

cues.speaker: ER
cues.text: It's mainly clerical and admin jobs they deal with, isn't it?

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: That's right.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: I know you're hoping to find a full-time job in the media eventually – but Becky mostly

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: recruits temporary staff for the finance sector – which will look good on your CV – and

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: generally pays better too.

cues.speaker: ER
cues.text: Yeah – I'm just a bit worried because I don't have much office experience.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: I wouldn't worry. They'll probably start you as a receptionist, or something like that.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: So what's important for that kind of job isn't so much having business skills or knowing

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: lots of different computer systems – it's communication that really matters – so you'd be

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: fine there. And you'll pick up office skills really quickly on the job.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: It's not that complicated.

cues.speaker: ER
cues.text: OK good. So how long do people generally need temporary staff for?

cues.speaker: ER
cues.text: It would be great if I could get something lasting at least a month.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: That shouldn't be too difficult.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: But you're more likely to be offered something for a week at first, which might get

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: extended. It's unusual to be sent somewhere for just a day or two.

cues.speaker: ER
cues.text: Right, I've heard the pay isn't too bad – better than working in a shop or a restaurant.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: Oh yes – definitely. The hourly rate is about £10, 11 if you're lucky.

cues.speaker: ER
cues.text: That's pretty good. I was only expecting to get eight or nine pounds an hour.
